title: LLM Deployment Thermometer — 2-Week Sprint Plan & Live Decision Ledger
body:
OVERVIEW:
This is a compact, execution-focused 2-week sprint plan for a customer POC to validate a low-latency, cost-bounded LLM deployment in a VPC (private) mode. The 'thermometer' metaphor is used to track heat (risk), cold-path fallbacks, and whether we hit latency/cost thresholds.

GOAL: get a production-feel inference pipeline running with a real workload, prove 99th-percentile latency < 220ms for single-turn text generation at target QPS, and show unit cost reductions from caching/batching >= 20% versus naive per-request inference.

SUCCESS METRICS (explicit):
- 99p latency <= 220ms (hosted-like policy)
- Avg token cost <= $0.0009/token OR 20% lower than baseline
- Rollout runbook that moves from canary -> full within 48h of sign-off
- Regression tests: perplexity drift < 3% on holdout prompt set

AUDIENCE: customer infra + app engineers, platform/SRE, solutions-engineering lead.

ASSUMPTIONS:
- Customer provides sample workload replay (S3) and accept list of 200 canonical prompts by day 2.
- Access to customer VPC and keys done day 1–2 (we have template IAM + CNI).

TWO-WEEK TIMELINE (high-level):
Week 0 (pre-sprint, owner: SE PM)
- Share pre-checklist and environment template (Asha).
- Create JIRA epic and baseline cost projection (ENG-4291).

Day 1 (kickoff) — Environment Onboard (owners: Asha / Diego)
- Kickoff call 9:30am PT, confirm target QPS and latency SLOs.
- Exchange VPC peering info, KMS thumbprints.
- Action: Diego to create private deployment cluster and attach sample GPU pool.
- Deliverable: baseline inference job + smoke test (generate 'hello world' with model v0).

Day 2 — Data + Prompt Set (owners: customer + Evelyn)
- Customer uploads replay logs (S3) and canonical prompts.
- Action: Evelyn runs workload profiler on a 1-hour sample to extract sequence length distribution.
- Decision point: pick quantization profile (float16 vs int8) — default to float16 until latency confirmed.

Day 3 — Baseline Run + Telemetry (owner: SRE contact)
- Baseline 1: no batching, no cache. Collect token-level latency, GPU utilization, cost estimate.
- Confirm tracing and logs are forwarded to Console (route: se/pilot/<customer>).

Day 4 — Smart Routing + Cache Prototype (owner: Samir)
- Implement prefix-KV cache for repeated warm prompts. Run A/B traffic split 50/50 to measure unit cost delta.
- Milestone: show >= 10% cost drop from caching on sample set.

Day 5 — Workshop: Tuning Session (owners: All)
- 60-minute deep-dive on batching window, max_batch_size, and kernel selection heuristics.
- Produce tuning matrix (sequence length vs batch size vs latency).

Day 6–8 — Canary Stress + Fallbacks (owner: Diego)
- Run spike scenarios (2x, 4x QPS) and verify autoscaling thresholds.

Day 9 — Quality & Regression Checks (owner: Evelyn)
- Run eval harness on canonical prompts, collect output drift, and human-check 20 samples.

Day 10 — Rollout Dry Run (owner: Asha)
- Execute canary rollout to 10% of traffic with automatic fallback to hosted variant if latency > 300ms for 1m.

Day 11–12 — Buffer & Documentation
- Finalize runbook, handoff notes, and cost report.

Day 13 — Executive Demo (owner: Asha)
- 30-min demo showing latency dashboards, cost delta, and runbook steps.

Day 14 — Closeout + Handoff (owners: All)
- Sign-off, transfer ticket ownership to customer success + infra, create Dedicated offer quote if customer wants committed capacity.

TASK TRACKER (compact):
- [ ] env-template: share VPC/CNI checklist (Asha) — due Day 0
- [ ] create-epic: JIRA epic and sprint (Asha) — due Day 0
- [ ] cluster-provision (Diego) — due Day 1
- [ ] profiler-run (Evelyn) — due Day 2
- [ ] baseline-infer (SRE) — due Day 3
- [ ] cache-proto (Samir) — due Day 4
- [ ] tuning-matrix (All) — due Day 5
- [ ] stress-tests (Diego) — due Day 6
- [ ] eval-harness (Evelyn) — due Day 9
- [ ] canary-rollout (Asha) — due Day 10
- [ ] runbook-doc (Asha) — due Day 12

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (customer-facing):
- Documented baseline and tuned ingest that meets the latency and cost thresholds above.
- Automated regression test that runs in CI and flags >3% quality drift.
- Handoff runbook with clear rollback and fallback to hosted variant.

RISK REGISTER (quick thermometer):
- VPC connectivity issues (heat: high) — mitigation: parallel host-mode fallback and temporary jump-host; escalate to infra on call.
- Model quality regression after quantization (heat: medium-high) — mitigation: keep float16 baseline; run diff eval before canary.
- Autoscaler overshoot causing cold starts (heat: medium) — mitigation: pre-warm policy and modest min-instances.
- Cost exceed projection due to long sequences (heat: medium) — mitigation: enforce token caps and sample-based reranking to reduce length.

WORKSHOP AGENDA (30–60m blocks):
- Intro & goals (10m)
- Baseline telemetry walkthrough (10m)
- Live tuning on caching/batching (20m)
- Decision ledger & open questions (10m)

DECISION LEDGER (live entries):
- [2025-11-04] Choose float16 as default; evaluate int8 in parallel (owner: Evelyn).
- [2025-11-04] Canary fallback policy: hosted-variant fallback after 1m of 99p > 300ms (owner: Asha).
- [2025-11-06] Enable prefix caching for exact-match prompts only in first pass (owner: Samir).

KICKOFF NOTES (from 2025-11-04 meeting):
- Customer uses replay with long-tail docs; median sequence length = 42, 80th = 210 (Evelyn).
- Primary KPI: interactivity for agents UI — must feel like <300ms for 95% of actions.
- Customer hesitant on int8 until we show quality regressions are within tolerance.
- Action item: customer to provide SOC contacts and compliance checklist by Day 3.

RESOURCE ESTIMATES (rough):
- GPU hours: 120 (NVIDIA A10-equivalent) for tuning and stress tests across 2 weeks.
- Eng effort: SE lead 0.3 FTE, SRE 0.2 FTE, ML engineer 0.3 FTE.

POST-PILOT DELIVERABLES:
- Slide: results + cost delta table (to share with customer)
- Runbook: step-by-step canary -> 100% rollout with rollback playbook
- PR: infra-as-code for the deployment (github PR linked above)

NOTES TO SELF (informal):
- Keep telemetry windows narrow during canary to detect regressions quickly.
- If customer refuses VPC peering, prepare a private-hosted compromise (dedicated capacity with VPC-like isolation).
- Remember to add local proxy to trace headers so we can attribute tail latency to network vs serving.

CONTACTS AND COMM CHANNELS:
- Slack channel: #se-pilot-llm-thermometer (create on Day 0)
- On-call infra: infra-oncall@redwood.ai (pager)
- Confluence blueprint: linked above

END OF DOCUMENT — this should live as the working sprint plan and decision ledger. Keep it lightweight; spin a new document if we move to a multi-customer playbook.
